chapter: Complaints to Senator Eastland, FCC and WDSU
title: La Rocca's January 1957 letter to WDSU's manager asking for the script
summary: The letter protests statements by Armand Hug and an announcer about the band, says Edwards did not keep the books, and cites his exhibits.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: All right. All right. All right. All right. You guys in? Yes, this is a letter from D. James, Nick LaRocca, 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans, Louisiana, 13, January 13, 1957. Mr. Swayze, manager, WDSU television station, 520 Royal Street City. Dear Mr. Swayze, the purpose of this letter is to request of you a script on a program. Read the supposed history of jazz as told through the facilities of WDDU. WDSU. WDSU. WDSU by Armand Hull and one of your announcers. This program happened around August of 1955. This program was in conjunction with the advertising, some motor car. Before this program had taken the air, I had sent your historian the following letter. 된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된된 as I am particularly interested in this matter being the manager and leader of the world's first jazz band, the original Dixieland jazz band, so I can refute any untruthful statements about me or the ODJB otherwise propaganda. I am of the opinion the Federal Radio Commission has control of this matter, etc. This letter was never answered. Any of the statements by your Mr. Hugg and announcer was untrue, especially the kind of music we played, also that Mr. Edwards kept the books for the band. I hadn't even been the leader and manager of this band, collected all the money for band, secured all engagements for band. This was done to humiliate me among my friends. Over your station, you say you abide with the National Television Code. I would not call this abiding by the code when you will give out pure pro-Negro lies to humiliate a person and take away the credit that belongs to the ODJB. Go speak to Orlans. Who was christened by the people of Chicago the first jazz band. No Negro music was called jazz. In my early days, the Negro music was ragtime. I have always thought that the airwaves were for the public service for all the people. But when it becomes a mere propaganda device for certain persons or factions or organizations, interesting in doing the thinking and judging and acting for the people, it ceases to be a public service, but becomes a mere propaganda device. I thought it was in Russia that this kind of propaganda was being used against some people. But it has come to New Orleans and put to use here. That helped this country if this programming is to be continued. The perusal of these photostat copies will tell you these carpetbaggers are liars. Exhibit 1, engagement in Chicago, 1916. Exhibit 2, opening New York City, and Rouse and Webbers, Exhibit 3. Victor released March 7, 1917, which was heard around the world and had perpetuated this music over the world before these modern carpetbaggers and self-appointed prophets were dry behind their ears. Exhibit 4, Tom Spicciune will tell how prevalent this music was in New Orleans in 1918. Marshall Stern, self-appointed prophet of jazz music, mocked Exhibit 5, Dr. Sue Sean Letta, Exhibit 6, Exhibit 7, Pete Rendler, the other billing is to show where we played, etc. I would have taken this matter up soon, but I have a family of six children to feed and could not devote much time to combating these liars. Now that I am partially retired, can find time to catch up on my writing of letters, where were all this great Negro music you speak of when we were in the spotlight? I had no competition until seven years after our record releases. Hoping I am favored with this script that was used on this program. Sincerely, I was organizer, leader and manager, the original Dixieland Jazz Band, creators of jazz music now in return. Now you have something typed on the bottom. No, don't put that in. Don't put that in.
